# Tokyo 5-Day Trip Plan: Apr 10–14, 2026

A practical 5-day Tokyo stay for **2 adults** with a **$1,200 lodging budget** works best in **Ueno, Shinjuku, or Asakusa**. These areas balance station access, hotel choice, and easy sightseeing.

## Recommended Neighborhoods and Stay Strategy

| Neighborhood | Best for | Why it fits | Budget fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ueno | First-time visitors, easy transit | Near Ueno Station, good hotel value, simple airport access | Strong |
| Shinjuku | Nightlife, central base, many train lines | Best all-around convenience, but prices can rise fast | Medium |
| Asakusa | Traditional Tokyo, calmer evenings | Good value, walkable, easy Metro access | Strong |
| Tokyo Station/Marunouchi | Business-style comfort, premium transit | Excellent rail access, usually pricier | Weak-to-medium |

## Ranked Hotel Search Targets

Option 1: **Ueno business hotel near station** | Best value for your budget; prioritize 3-star or compact 4-star rooms | Near Ueno Station, non-smoking, Wi‑Fi, breakfast add-on or included
Action: [Button: Search Ueno] https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Ueno%2C%20Tokyo%2C%20Japan

Option 2: **Asakusa hotel near subway** | Good mix of price, walkability, and sightseeing access | Non-smoking rooms are common; breakfast often available
Action: [Button: Search Asakusa] https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Asakusa%2C%20Tokyo%2C%20Japan

Option 3: **Shinjuku hotel near station** | Best for transit flexibility and dining, but watch rates | Filter for “free Wi‑Fi” and “breakfast included” to stay on budget
Action: [Button: Search Shinjuku] https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Shinjuku%2C%20Tokyo%2C%20Japan

Option 4: **Tokyo Station area hotel** | Most convenient for rail connections, least budget-friendly | Consider only if you find a strong deal early
Action: [Button: Search Tokyo Station] https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Tokyo%20Station%2C%20Tokyo%2C%20Japan

Day 1: **Arrival + Easy West Tokyo**

- Afternoon: Explore **Shinjuku Gyoen** or a nearby neighborhood stroll.
- Dinner: Simple ramen or izakaya near your hotel.

Action: [Button: Map It] https://www.google.com/maps/search/Tokyo+hotel+near+station

Day 2: **Classic Tokyo Core**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

- Afternoon: **Ginza** shopping streets and café break.
- Dinner: Sushi or tempura in central Tokyo.

Action: [Button: Plan Route] https://www.google.com/maps/search/Tokyo+Station+to+Ginza

Day 3: **Asakusa and Ueno**

- Afternoon: **Ueno Park** and one museum of your choice.
Media: Alt=Afternoon: **Ueno Park** and one museum of your choice, Tokyo, Japan

Action: [Button: Open Area Guide] https://www.google.com/maps/search/Asakusa+Ueno+Tokyo

- Dinner: Casual dinner in Shibuya or Shinjuku.

Action: [Button: Explore Route] https://www.google.com/maps/search/Shibuya+Harajuku+Tokyo

- Dinner: Use this as your travel meal window if your flight is late.

Action: [Button: Final Day Options] https://www.google.com/maps/search/Tokyo+half+day+itinerary

## Lodging Budget Fit

| Stay Style | Typical Nightly Target | 4 Nights Total | Fit for $1,200 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Value business hotel | $120–$180 | $480–$720 | Excellent |
| Mid-range station hotel | $180–$250 | $720–$1,000 | Good |
| Premium central hotel | $250–$350+ | $1,000–$1,400+ | Tight |

Aiming for **$150–$220 per night** gives you the best chance of getting:
- non-smoking room
- free Wi‑Fi
- breakfast included or available
- station access without overspending

## Flight and Hotel Booking Checklist

### Flights
- Book flights first if your dates are fixed.
- Compare arrival into **HND (Haneda)** and **NRT (Narita)**; Haneda is usually more convenient.
- Choose flights that land earlier on **Apr 10** and depart later on **Apr 14** to reduce hotel-night waste.
- Check baggage rules carefully if you are comparing basic economy fares.
- Try to keep at least one buffer hour for immigration and rail transfer.

### Hotel
- Filter for **“near station”**, **“non-smoking”**, **“free Wi‑Fi”**, and **“breakfast included”**.
- Check whether breakfast is truly included or only available as an add-on.
- Confirm room size; Tokyo rooms can be compact.
- Look for cancellation flexibility until flights are fully locked.
- Read recent reviews for cleanliness, noise, and air-conditioning.

### Best booking order
- Book **flights first** if fares are rising.
- Book **hotel second** once you know your airport and arrival time.
- If a hotel has a strong free-cancellation rate and fits the budget, reserve it early.

## Quick Actions
